entries.title: US, South Korea and Japan Renew Commitment to North Korea’s Denuclearization
entries.paragraph_1: The United States, South Korea and Japan have renewed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible nuclear talks with Washington. Speculation has grown over a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, following repeated overtures by Trump for renewed nuclear negotiations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi reaffirmed their position during a meeting on Friday on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) gathering in Atlanta, Georgia. Advertisement According to the US State Department, the three officials “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea. They also pledged to ensure the “full implementation” of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including measures prohibiting support for revenue-generating activities linked to North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Despite years of international sanctions, North Korea, which enjoys support from Russia and China, has legally entrenched its status as a nuclear-armed state. Its government has repeatedly insisted that its nuclear arsenal is permanent and irreversible. Advertisement Trump open to meeting Kim Trump has repeatedly expressed willingness to engage Pyongyang in nuclear negotiations while reducing joint military exercises with South Korea, a key US ally. The US president departed from longstanding American policy last year when he acknowledged that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”. He also signalled that he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim, although the North Korean leader did not respond to the proposal. Advertisement Analysts and South Korea’s intelligence agency believe Kim may have communicated Pyongyang’s position on possible talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong. South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung, who has adopted a more conciliatory approach towards Pyongyang, has repeatedly called for dialogue without preconditions. In September, Lee suggested that Washington consider pursuing a freeze on North Korea’s nuclear programme rather than demanding its immediate dismantlement, in exchange for sanctions relief. Advertisement However, critics argue that such a proposal could amount to tacit recognition of North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to secure sanctions relief without surrendering its weapons. Some analysts also believe China may be moving towards accepting North Korea’s nuclear status, citing the absence of references to denuclearisation in statements issued after Kim met Chinese President Xi Jinping in June. Meanwhile, Pyongyang on Saturday criticised a joint statement issued by a group of countries monitoring the implementation of sanctions against it. Advertisement North Korea insisted that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”. entries.title: North Korea answers South’s proposal for military talks by firing off ballistic missiles
entries.paragraph_1: North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, 17 days after its previous ballistic missile launch on Oct. 12. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the projectile launches from the Wonsan area around 12:30 pm. The launches came six days after South Korea’s Ministry of National Defense proposed military talks with North Korea on Oct. 23 to prevent accidental clashes along the Military Demarcation Line following recent land mine explosions in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). According to the Joint Chiefs, the missiles traveled around 250 kilometers. South Korean and US authorities are currently analyzing the technical details. The missiles were reportedly among a range of weapons systems — including 600 mm super-large multiple rocket launchers — that North Korean forces drilled on Thursday. South Korea’s National Security Office convened an emergency meeting with officials from the Defense Ministry, the Joint Chiefs and other relevant agencies to review the security situation. “We emphasized the need to thoroughly assess the implications of the launches for our security and ensure that all necessary measures are taken,” an office spokesperson said after the meeting. The office also urged North Korea to immediately halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, calling them “violations of UN Security Council resolutions and grave actions that do nothing to help contain the current situation.”
entries.paragraph_2: By Jang Na-rye, staff reporter; Kwon Hyuk-chul, staff reporter

entries.paragraph_1: South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy released October 2026 export data Sunday to figures that would have been implausible at any prior point in the country's industrial history: semiconductor shipments reached $56.4 billion for the month, an increase of 259.4% from October 2025, and accounted for 48.9% of all South Korean goods exported — making chips nearly one dollar out of every two that left the country. Total exports across all categories hit $115.3 billion, a 93.7% year-on-year gain and the highest October figure in the country's history, extending a streak of monthly records that has turned 2026 into the most extraordinary year for Korean trade in modern memory.
entries.paragraph_2: The driver is structural, not cyclical. South Korea produces an estimated 80–90% of the world's High Bandwidth Memory — the specialized, stacked-DRAM architecture that AI accelerators require to perform inference at scale — and demand for that memory has grown in direct proportion to the global AI infrastructure buildout. As hyperscalers spend hundreds of billions of dollars expanding AI data center capacity, every GPU they deploy must be paired with HBM that, with very few exceptions, can only come from South Korea.

entries.paragraph_2: Merz, leading a high-level 30-strong business delegation, visited Singapore, South Korea and Japan. The focus was on so-called “de-risking”—opening up new markets and investment opportunities to replace the deteriorating economic relations with China and, though this is less openly discussed, to curb US influence.

entries.title: South Korea Boosts Russian Coal Purchases in 2026
entries.paragraph_1: In brief: South Korea increased imports of Russian coal by 34% from January to August, up 34% from the same period in 2025, energy think tank CREA said. It attributed the 18 million metric ton rise to increased coal-fired power generation to offset nuclear power losses following the expiration of reactor licenses. South Korea ranked fourth among destinations for Russian coal exports.
entries.paragraph_2: South Korea raised coal imports from Russia in the first eight months of 2026, Finland-based energy think tank Centre for Research on Energy and Clear Air (CREA) said.

entries.title: The country probably deserves better | Philstar.com
entries.paragraph_1: As Semirara Mining and Power Corp.’s 50-year coal-operating contract with the government for Semirara Island in Antique approaches expiration next year, a number of questions have been raised by SMPC about the propriety of auctioning the Semirara coal blocks.
entries.paragraph_2: In February, the government rejected SMPC’s bid to extend its coal operating contract for an additional 13 years, after the Department of Justice opined that constitutional and legal limits cap the maximum duration of such natural resource agreements at 50 years.
